description: The plot illustrates how two metrics—perplexity and GPU memory ratio—vary as a function of the recent sequence ratio. The x-axis is labeled “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)” on a linear scale, spanning roughly 10% to 100% with labeled ticks at 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100. The left y-axis is labeled “Perplexity” on a linear scale from about 4.2 to 4.7 with ticks at 0.1 increments, and the right y-axis is labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio (%)” on a linear scale from 40% to 100% with ticks every 10%. One orange solid line with circular markers labeled “Perplexity” starts near 4.59 at 10%, decreases through about 4.45 (20%), 4.39 (30%), and reaches a low around 4.30 at 40%, then rises to about 4.33 (50%) and 4.34 (60%), dips to about 4.29 at 70%, increases to about 4.33 at 80%, peaks near 4.39 at 90%, and ends around 4.38 at 100%; a red dashed horizontal reference line labeled “Full Cache PPL” is drawn at approximately 4.38 across the full x-range. One blue solid line with circular markers labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio” begins around 41% at 10% and increases gradually to about 42% (20%), 43% (30%), 44% (40%), 45% (50%), 46% (60%), and about 48% (70%), then rises to roughly 55% at 80%, jumps sharply to about 98% at 90%, and ends near 99% at 100%; a blue dashed horizontal reference line labeled “Full Cache GPU Mem.” is drawn near 98% across the full x-range.
